paper.title: Analytic reproducibility in articles receiving open data badges at the journal Psychological Science: an observational study

judgement_checks.abstract_vs_body: Abstract: 37 major discrepancies out of 789 (5% [3,6]); Results p.4 same 37/789. But data_values.csv has MAJOR_ERROR 29 + DECISION_ERROR 1 = 30, and Rmd line 291 adds decisionErrors to majorErrors; 37 is not 29+1+7(EYEBALL_ERROR)=37 only if eyeball errors are counted as major

No parameter in the text contradicts the code.
judgement_checks.phantom_experiment: All analyses in the text have code: preprocessing.R, manuscript.Rmd, meta_analysis.R, plot_*.R; data_articles.csv (25 rows) and data_values.csv (789 rows) exist; SI sections C/E are in the supplementary Rmd, not in the capsule.
judgement_checks.figure_data_mismatch: Fig.1 forest plot is produced by meta_analysis.R from data_hardwicke2018 (35 rows) + articleLevelSummary; Fig.2/3 from data_values.csv; stored results/manuscript_files/figure-latex/*.png exist. judgement_checks.claims_scan: claims_scan.py found 0 candidate claims (paper is a descriptive observational study with no hypothesis-test claims); the 10 ledger claims were checked by hand against Abstract/Results/Table 1.

findings.location: Abstract vs Results p.4 vs data/raw/data_values.csv
findings.evidence: Paper: 37 major numerical discrepancies out of 789 (5%). data_values.csv comparisonOutcome counts: MAJOR_ERROR 29 + DECISION_ERROR 1 = 30; EYEBALL_ERROR 7; MINOR_ERROR 108; MATCH 644 (total 789). manuscript.Rmd:291 adds decisionErrors to majorErrors, so the code yields 30, not 37; 37 = 29+1+7 only if the 7 EYEBALL_ERROR rows are also counted as major. 30/789 = 3.8%, 37/789 = 4.7%.
findings.question_for_authors: Which rows are counted as major discrepancies: 30 (MAJOR_ERROR+DECISION_ERROR) or 37 (also EYEBALL_ERROR)?
